title: Imperial vs metric
examples: Teacher, how do I change feet to meters?
Is it always easier to use metric units?
What is the difference between a pound and a kilogram?

explain.say: Today we learn about two ways to measure things. One is called the imperial system. The other is called the metric system.
The metric system uses simple numbers and prefixes. For example, we use centimeters for small lengths. One hundred centimeters make one meter.
The imperial system uses different units for length and weight. For length, we use inches and feet. For weight, we use pounds.
To change between them, we use approximations. For example, six inches is about one hundred and five millimeters. Remember these common conversions.
When you are baking cookies, the recipe might call for cups of flour. If you only have grams, you need to convert the measurement. This shows when you use different units for the same thing.

faq.q: Why do we have two different systems?
faq.a: Some countries use the metric system for science. Other countries still use the imperial system for everyday life.
asks: Which system is better to use?
Why are there two ways to measure things?

faq.q: How do I convert inches to centimeters?
faq.a: You multiply the number of inches by two point five four. So, three inches times two point five four equals seven point six two centimeters.
asks: What is the conversion from inches to cm?
Can you show me inches to centimeters?

faq.q: Is a pound the same as a kilogram?
faq.a: No, they are not the same. A pound is a unit of weight in the imperial system. A kilogram is the unit in the metric system.
asks: What is the difference between pounds and kilograms?

faq.q: What is the relationship between feet and meters?
faq.a: One meter is approximately equal to three point two eight feet. This is a common approximation you should know.
asks: How many feet are in a meter?
What is the foot to meter conversion?

faq.q: Do I need to remember all the conversions?
faq.a: You only need to remember the most common ones for your class. We will focus on inches and pounds for now.
asks: Do I need to memorize everything?

facts: The metric system is widely used in science and many countries.
In the imperial system, a foot is made up of twelve inches.
One pound is approximately equal to zero point four five kilograms.
The metric system uses base units like meters and grams.

quiz.say: If something is three feet long, how many inches is that?
quiz.why: Because there are twelve inches in one foot, you multiply three by twelve to get thirty-six inches.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you subtract one instead of multiplying.
wrong.1: This is too high because you multiplied by one hundred instead of twelve.
wrong.3: This is only correct if the length was one foot.

quiz.say: What is the approximate length of six inches in centimeters?
quiz.why: Using the common approximation, six inches is equal to fifteen centimeters.

wrong.0: This is too low because you only used half of the correct factor.
wrong.1: This mistake happens if you just use the number six without converting.
wrong.2: This is too high because you multiplied by ten instead of the correct factor.

quiz.say: If a bag weighs two pounds, approximately how many kilograms is that?
quiz.why: Since one pound is about zero point four five kilograms, two pounds is close to zero point nine kilograms.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you multiply by one instead of the correct conversion factor.
wrong.2: This assumes that pounds and kilograms are the same unit of weight.
wrong.3: This is only correct if the bag weighed just one pound.
